title: Choose the passive
instructions: Read the active sentence. Then tap the pendulum with the verb form that completes it in the passive.

rounds.active: The new firm is designing our head office in Lisbon.
rounds.note: The active is present continuous (is designing), so the passive keeps it: is being + past participle.
A finished past time (in 1998) needs the past simple passive: was/were + past participle.

rounds.active: Somebody cleans the offices every evening.
rounds.note: A routine (every evening) is present simple; plural offices, so are + past participle.

rounds.active: They will announce the results tomorrow.
rounds.note: Will + be + past participle. 'Will announce' is still active — the results don't announce anything.

rounds.active: They are going to open a new school next year.
rounds.note: Keep 'going to' and add be + past participle: is going to be opened.

rounds.active: They were repairing the road when we arrived.
rounds.note: The repair was in progress when we arrived: past continuous passive, was being + past participle.
A past action with a result now (the bike is gone): has/have been + past participle.

rounds.active: By six o'clock they had cleaned the whole house.
rounds.passive: By six o'clock the whole house ___.
rounds.note: 'By six o'clock' marks a point in the past before which it was done: had been + past participle.

rounds.active: The builders will have finished the stadium by May.
rounds.note: 'By May' looks back from a future point: will have been + past participle.

rounds.active: You must wear a helmet on the building site.
rounds.passive: A helmet ___ on the building site.
rounds.note: Modal + be + past participle. 'Must wear' is active; 'must being' is never possible.

rounds.active: They can't finish the project on time.
rounds.note: Can't + be + past participle. After a modal the verb is always the bare form: be, never been or being.

rounds.active: Someone should have told us earlier.
rounds.note: A past criticism: should have been + past participle. The person told is now the subject.

rounds.active: They might have cancelled the concert.
rounds.note: A guess about the past: might have been + past participle.

rounds.active: A mechanic is going to check my car.
rounds.passive: I'm going to ___ my car checked.
rounds.note: Have + object + past participle: someone else does the job for you — I'm going to have my car checked.

rounds.active: The hairdresser cut my hair yesterday.
rounds.note: Past causative: had + object + past participle. 'I cut my hair' would mean you did it yourself.

rounds.active: People say that he is a millionaire.
rounds.note: People say (now) → he is said; the belief is about now, so 'to be'.

rounds.active: People believe the painting was stolen in 1990.
rounds.passive: The painting ___ to have been stolen in 1990.
rounds.note: The belief is now (is believed); the theft was earlier, so 'to have been stolen'.
